note: One expectation index per contract directory. Each case names the structural violations that prove its point as (pointer, keyword) pairs; a validator's free-text message is deliberately never recorded. The expected set must be a subset of what the validator reports, because a conditional rule often reports a broader violation alongside the specific one.

state-seventh-value.proves: The global vocabulary is closed at six values. A seventh operational-sounding state is not a run state, however reasonable it looks; adding one is a product decision, not a document a producer may simply send.

state-pr5-requested.proves: REQUESTED was a global state in the superseded nineteen-state model. It cannot re-enter through a document even though no Python constant names it any more.

state-pr5-ready.proves: READY described report readiness, not execution. Coupling execution state to release readiness is exactly the conflation this contract exists to prevent.

state-stage-like-scoring.proves: A stage or business phase is not a global execution state. A stage's progress belongs in its own record, which this document never embeds.

state-lowercase.proves: The vocabulary is case-sensitive, so a lowercased token cannot be matched against an approved state by accident.

terminal-without-finished-at.proves: A terminal state states when the run finished. Without it a consumer cannot tell a finished run from one whose end was never recorded.

non-terminal-with-finished-at.proves: The converse rule: a run that is still executing has no end instant, so finished_at is refused rather than tolerated as harmless extra data.

failed-without-failure.proves: A failed run says why in machine-readable terms. A bare FAILED with no code leaves a consumer nothing to branch on.

failure-on-succeeded.proves: Failure metadata belongs to FAILED alone. A succeeded or cancelled run carrying a failure code would make the state member unreliable as the single answer to how the run ended.

failure-carries-detail.proves: The failure block is a code and nothing else. A detail member is precisely the channel through which a traceback, an exception message or a filesystem path would reach a client.

failure-stage-property.proves: A failure is not attributed to a stage here. Naming the stage that failed would make the global state a projection of stage outcomes, which this slice deliberately does not decide.

customer-release-property.proves: SUCCEEDED is an execution fact only. A customer_release member would couple finishing execution to releasing a result to a customer, and the root is closed so the coupling cannot be bolted on.

stage-executions-property.proves: Stage executions are not embedded in the run state. The two documents are linked by run_id alone, so neither can be derived from the other by reading one of them.
